Meeting header: 2026-10-06 16:00 PDT | Duration 48m | Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Tom Rivera (Redwood SE), Jade Park (Redwood Product), Sujata Rao (BrightSearch), Mark Li (BrightSearch), Evan Ortiz (BrightSearch)

[00:00] Alice Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining uh we can do a quick intro round real fast um and then i'll hand over to tom for the demo.
[00:08] Sujata Rao: yeah thanks alice, i'm sujata, i run search at brightsearch, uh our main problem is results quality after migrating to a vector-first architecture and we want better reranking for long-tail queries.
[00:20] Mark Li: Mark, eng lead on search; we manage the infra and latency targets.
[00:25] Evan Ortiz: Evan PM, prioritizing relevance metrics for q4.
[00:30] Alice Chen: great, quick agenda: embeddings walkthrough, rerank endpoint demo in the console and via the hosted API, then discuss perf/cost and security. Tom?
[00:39] Tom Rivera: sweet, i'll share screen - okay, so high level flow we typically recommend: embed your corpus with the embeddings endpoint (we use redwood-embed-v1 in the demo), store vectors in your vector DB, embed the query, compute top-k candidates by similarity, and then optionally call our rerank endpoint which takes the candidates plus the original query and returns a re-scored ordering.
[01:05] Tom Rivera: i'm going to show a small notebook - apologies if the auto-transcript is messy - so first cell: call embeddings.create with model redwood-embed-v1, we do batching of 64 here, you can tune batch size based on payload size and latency constraints.
[01:22] Jade Park: just to add, Redwood Optimize will suggest batching and quantization profiles based on your historical traffic if you enable telemetry - it's optional but it really helps unit cost.
[01:33] Sujata Rao: quick q: if we embed on write, what's the expectation for updates? we have frequent doc edits.
[01:40] Tom Rivera: good question - typical pattern is incremental upserts for changed docs, and if you need near-perfect coherence you can do periodic re-embeds for hot docs; Redwood also supports prefix/KV cache that'll reduce cost for conversational flows, less impact on static corpus.
[02:05] Speaker 3: can you show the actual rerank payload?
[02:08] Tom Rivera: sure, here's an example - we send query string, an array of candidate doc ids + their embeddings, and a context snippet; if you pass raw docs we can compute embeddings server-side but for scale we recommend client-side embedding and passing vectors.
[02:25] Tom Rivera: demo time - search for "enterprise billing issues" -> base retrieval returns 12 candidates, top 5 similarity scores roughly similar, rerank endpoint applies a learned reranker (it uses model variant redwood-rerank-1, tuned for retrieval signals) and returns an ordered list with new scores. you'll see precision@5 bump in this toy set.
[02:50] Sujata Rao: nice, what's the latency on that rerank call for 5 candidates?
[02:55] Tom Rivera: in hosted API regions we generally see 40-120ms for a 5-candidate rerank with redwood-rerank-1 in a standard config, depends on sequence length of snippets; if candidates include long docs it can be higher.
[03:10] Mark Li: that's fine but our P95 end-to-end needs to stay under 200ms for web search - so combining retrieval + rerank + network we need to plan.
[03:18] Tom Rivera: totally - retrieval should be extremely fast if you use an optimized vectordb like Pinecone or your local OpenSearch vector plugin. And Redwood supports async rerank via background scoring or synchronous depending on your SLO. We can also do an approach where you show top-n with a cheap embedding sim and then re-rank on user interaction.
[03:37] Evan Ortiz: cost question - embeddings for 1M docs looks expensive unless we compress or quantize.
[03:44] Jade Park: right - Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and smaller embed models for cold documents; you can also do hybrid: coarse embed index for first-pass and higher-fidelity reranker for top-k. That reduces per-token costs for reranking.
[03:58] Speaker 2: are there limits on vector size?
[04:01] Tom Rivera: models currently provide 768 or 1024 dims depending on model; we support z-score normalization client-side, no enforced limits beyond payload size and practical storage.
[04:14] Alice Chen: switching over to the Console - you can see per-route dashboards, token level cost breakdowns, and a rerank telemetry view that shows before/after metrics on precision/ctr, that's been helpful to Ship teams.
[04:30] Tom Rivera: demo: console >> APIs >> rerank logs, here's a sample where we pushed a canary with redwood-rerank-1-v2 and compared to baseline. You can configure canary rollouts and automatic fallback if quality drops, which is handy for production.
[04:50] Sujata Rao: security - we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), and audit logs. Also data residency in EU for a subset of traffic.
[04:58] Alice Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified; we support SSO/SAML and RBAC and can provide audit logs. For EU residency we have regions that can be pinned at account level or you can use private deployment for stricter controls. We'll attach the security pack after the call.
[05:15] Mark Li: encryption at rest - do you manage keys or can bring our KMS?
[05:20] Jade Park: both - hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default, but enterprise Private supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). We'll mark that on the security doc.
[05:28] Evan Ortiz: curious about model drift detection for rerank - do you track evals?
[05:33] Tom Rivera: yes, Redwood Optimize supports automated evals against your prompt sets and can alert on regressions; you can hook it to your test queries and get regression alerts.
[05:42] Alice Chen: real quick, let's run a live A/B: baseline retrieval vs retrieval + rerank on a small test set. Tom are you able to run the notebook end to end?
[05:50] Tom Rivera: yep, running now - embedding batch 128 for corpus, query embed for set of 10 queries, compute cosine top-20, then call rerank with top-5.
[06:05] Tom Rivera: okay results for first query: baseline precision@5 0.56, after rerank 0.78, sample ranking change shows the more context-aware snippets moving up.
[06:20] Sujata Rao: those gains look promising. How comparable are these numbers on real traffic?
[06:25] Tom Rivera: depends on corpus and query distribution; that's why we recommend a pilot where we run your 1k query set and measure improvements and latency.
[06:33] Speaker 4: do you support streaming rerank or partial scores?
[06:37] Tom Rivera: rerank is not streamed today - it's a synchronous call which returns final scores. For very low-latency scenarios we recommend async background re-scoring or edge-side cheap re-rank.
[06:48] Mark Li: any quotas or throughput caps on hosted? we need sustained 200 qps for retrieval and 30 qps for rerank during peak.
[06:56] Alice Chen: hosted has configurable rate limits and we do offer Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput (reserved GPU pools) if you need that SLA. For pilot, hosted should be fine; if you commit to Dedicated we can reserve capacity.
[07:12] Evan Ortiz: priceballpark for that throughput?
[07:15] Alice Chen: i'll follow up with a tiered pricing deck - rough numbers in the deck we sent last week, but we prefer to size based on your bench results.
[07:25] Tom Rivera: also note caching - if many queries share prefixes or context we can use prefix caching and KV cache to reduce compute.
[07:40] Sujata Rao: legal/contracts - do you accept standard enterprise amendments?
[07:44] Alice Chen: yes we usually accept standard enterprise amendments, can work with procurement. We'll share sample contracts.
[07:50] Jade Park: small note on model selection: redwood-embed-v1 is a good general-purpose embedder; for specialized domain data we can recommend fine-tuning or using a different embedding model size. The reranker can also be tuned on your labeled pairs.
[08:05] Tom Rivera: running a second query - here's an example where rerank reduced click-through time by surfacing the exact doc.
[08:18] Mark Li: for logs and privacy, can we redact PII in logs before sending to Redwood?
[08:22] Alice Chen: yes you can scrub logs client-side; we also have retention controls and can restrict which artifacts are sent to Redwood.
[08:33] Evan Ortiz: demo looked good, what would a pilot timeline look like?
[08:36] Alice Chen: typical pilot is 4 weeks: week 1 integration and data ingest (1k docs), week 2 run baselines and tune, week 3 evaluate and iterate, week 4 wrap up and decide expansion to Dedicated. We'll propose exact timeline after we see your test set.
[08:52] Tom Rivera: dropping links in chat - demo notebook: github.com/redwood/demo/embeddings-rerank, benchmark csv, and a short README.
[09:00] Sujata Rao: excellent. quick technical - can rerank use external signals (clicks) as features?
[09:06] Tom Rivera: yes you can pass metadata and click features per candidate; the reranker accepts additional tokenized features, but you may need a small engineering shim to include them in the payload.
[09:20] Speaker 1: transcription glitch - 'KV cash' lol - meant KV cache.
[09:25] (laughter)
[09:30] Alice Chen: ok wrapping up, recap of what we promised: pricing + security docs, notebook + benchmark, sample contract, and pilot kickoff. Any final blockers?
[09:42] Mark Li: just internal signoffs; we'll need to confirm budget next week.
[09:46] Sujata Rao: also want success metrics: 10-15% lift in p@5 and sub-200ms P95 end-to-end.
[09:53] Alice Chen: noted - we'll include that in the pilot SOW.
[09:57] Evan Ortiz: thanks all, looking forward to the next steps.
[09:59] Alice Chen: thanks everyone - we'll follow up via email and slack. End meeting.
